Accounting
Accounting is the process of recording, summarizing, analyzing, and reporting financial transactions
of a business or organization. It provides essential information about financial performance and
position, helping stakeholders make informed decisions.
The main purpose of accounting is to track income, expenses, assets, and liabilities. This
information is used to prepare financial statements such as the income statement, balance sheet,
and cash flow statement. These reports provide insights into profitability, financial stability, and
cash management.
There are different types of accounting, including financial accounting, management accounting,
and auditing. Financial accounting focuses on external reporting, while management accounting
provides internal insights for decision

Accounting follows standardized principles such as Generally Accepted Accounting Principles
(GAAP) or International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS). These standards ensure
consistency and transparency in financial reporting across organizations.
Technology has significantly transformed accounting practices. Software tools automate
calculations, reduce errors, and improve efficiency. Cloud-based accounting systems allow
real-time access to financial data, enabling better collaboration and decision-making.

Information Technology
Information Technology (IT) refers to the use of computers, software, networks, and systems to
manage, process, and distribute information. It plays a vital role in modern society by enabling
communication, data storage, cybersecurity, and digital services. IT includes areas such as
hardware, software development, networking, cloud computing, and database management.
In today’s world, IT supports almost every industry including healthcare, education, finance, and
business operations. Organizations rely on IT systems to store large amounts of data, automate
processes, and improve efficiency. Technologies such as cloud computing allow companies to
store data remotely, reducing the need for physical infrastructure and enabling access from
anywhere.

Management
Management is the process of planning, organizing, leading, and controlling resources to achieve
organizational goals efficiently and effectively. It involves coordinating people, tasks, and processes
to ensure that objectives are met.
The four main functions of management are planning, organizing, leading, and controlling. Planning
involves setting goals and determining the best course of action. Organizing involves allocating
resources and assigning tasks. Leading focuses on motivating and guiding employees, while
controlling ensures that performance aligns with goals.
Managers play a key role in decision-making and problem-solving. They must analyze information,
evaluate alternatives, and choose the best solutions. Effective communication is essential for
coordinating activit

Leadership is an important aspect of management. Good leaders inspire and motivate employees,
foster teamwork, and create a positive work environment. Different leadership styles can be used
depending on the situation.
Technology has transformed management practices by providing tools for communication, data
analysis, and project management. Managers use software systems to monitor performance and
make informed decisions.
Ethics and responsibility are also important in management. Managers must ensure fairness,
transparency, and accountability in their actions.

TESOL
Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL) is the field of education focused on
teaching English to non-native speakers. It plays a crucial role in helping individuals communicate
effectively in English for academic, professional, and social purposes.
TESOL involves understanding language acquisition, teaching methods, and cultural differences.
Teachers use various approaches such as communicative language teaching, task-based learning,
and interactive activities to engage students and improve their language skills.
The main components of language learning include listening, speaking, reading, and writing.
TESOL programs aim to develop these skills through structured lessons and practical exercises.
Teachers also focus on grammar, vocabulary, pronunciation, and comprehen

Teachers also focus on grammar, vocabulary, pronunciation, and comprehension.
Cultural awareness is an important aspect of TESOL. Teachers must understand the backgrounds
of their students and adapt their teaching methods accordingly. This helps create an inclusive and
supportive learning environment.
Technology is increasingly used in TESOL. Online platforms, language apps, and multimedia
resources enhance learning and provide opportunities for practice outside the classroom. Virtual
classrooms enable students to learn from anywhere in the world.

Business
Business refers to the activity of producing, buying, and selling goods or services to meet customer
needs and generate profit. It plays a central role in economic development by creating jobs,
generating income, and contributing to the overall growth of society.
Businesses can be classified into different types such as sole proprietorships, partnerships,
corporations, and franchises. Each type has its own structure, advantages, and legal requirements.
Businesses operate in various industries including retail, manufacturing, services, and technology.
Key functions of a business include marketing, finance, operations, and human resources.
Marketing focuses on promoting products and understanding customer needs, while finance
manages money and investments. Operations ensure efficien

manages money and investments. Operations ensure efficient production and delivery of goods or
services, and human resources manage employees.
Effective decision-making is crucial for business success. Managers analyze market trends,
customer preferences, and financial data to make strategic decisions. Innovation and adaptability
are also important, as businesses must respond to changing market conditions.
Technology has become an integral part of modern business operations. Digital tools enable online
marketing, e-commerce, and data analysis. Businesses use technology to improve efficiency and
reach a global audience.

Information Systems
Information Systems (IS) are organized systems for collecting, processing, storing, and distributing
information to support decision-making and control within an organization. They combine
technology, people, and processes to manage data effectively.
An information system typically consists of hardware, software, databases, networks, and users.
These components work together to transform raw data into meaningful information. For example, a
business may use an information system to track sales, manage inventory, and generate reports.

Management Information Systems (MIS), Decision Support Systems (DSS), and Enterprise
